record.paper_title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
record.original_question: How do federated client-sampling constraints such as connection quality, device type, location, activity patterns, local dataset size, latency, and dropout affect fairness, and how can those impacts be mitigated through federated objectives, sampling, scheduling, or online-fairness methods?

artifact.category_tag: federated learning fairness and client sampling
artifact.status_search_result: Recent surveys and research papers (2024–2025) on fairness in federated learning explicitly identify client-sampling constraints (heterogeneity, partial participation, dropout, device/availability bias) as ongoing challenges. Proposed mitigations — fairness-constrained objectives, biased/lattice-based sampling, scheduling, and online fairness methods — are still being developed and benchmarked, with no comprehensive theoretical resolution. The problem is treated as open in the current literature.

status_evidence.title: Fairness in Federated Learning: Trends, Challenges, and Opportunities
status_evidence.snippet: Survey identifies client selection and partial participation as key open challenges for fairness in FL.
status_evidence.claim: Mitigating sampling-driven unfairness in FL remains an active open research area.

status_evidence.title: A survey on group fairness in federated learning (2025)
status_evidence.snippet: Partial participation and limited visibility into protected attributes make fairness difficult to measure or enforce during FL training.
status_evidence.claim: No comprehensive solution exists; multiple partial mitigations are proposed.

status_evidence.title: Federated Semi-Supervised Learning with Uniform Random and Lattice-Based Client Sampling
status_evidence.snippet: Lattice-based sampling reduces selection variance and bias from heterogeneity.
status_evidence.claim: Sampling-scheme-based mitigations are still being introduced and studied.
